3: //! Signal driver
4: 
5: use crate::io::driver::{Driver as IoDriver, Interest};
6: use crate::io::PollEvented;
7: use crate::park::Park;
8: use crate::signal::registry::globals;
9: 
10: use mio::net::UnixStream;
11: use std::io::{self, Read};
12: use std::ptr;
13: use std::sync::{Arc, Weak};
14: use std::task::{Context, Poll, RawWaker, RawWakerVTable, Waker};
15: use std::time::Duration;
16: 
17: /// Responsible for registering wakeups when an OS signal is received, and
18: /// subsequently dispatching notifications to any signal listeners as appropriate.
19: ///
20: /// Note: this driver relies on having an enabled IO driver in order to listen to
21: /// pipe write wakeups.
22: #[derive(Debug)]
23: pub(crate) struct Driver {
24:     /// Thread parker. The `Driver` park implementation delegates to this.
25:     park: IoDriver,
26: 
27:     /// A pipe for receiving wake events from the signal handler
28:     receiver: PollEvented<UnixStream>,
29: 
30:     /// Shared state
31:     inner: Arc<Inner>,
32: }
33: 
34: #[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
35: pub(crate) struct Handle {
36:     inner: Weak<Inner>,
37: }
38: 
39: #[derive(Debug)]
40: pub(super) struct Inner(());
41: 
42: // ===== impl Driver =====
43: 
44: impl Driver {
45:     /// Creates a new signal `Driver` instance that delegates wakeups to `park`.
46:     pub(crate) fn new(park: IoDriver) -> io::Result<Self> {
47:         use crate::io::driver::{Registration, ADDRESS, GENERATION};
48:         use crate::util::slab::Page;
49:         use std::mem::ManuallyDrop;
50:         use std::os::unix::io::{AsRawFd, FromRawFd};
51: 
52:         // NB: We give each driver a "fresh" receiver file descriptor to avoid
53:         // the issues described in alexcrichton/tokio-process#42.
54:         //
55:         // In the past we would reuse the actual receiver file descriptor and
56:         // swallow any errors around double registration of the same descriptor.
57:         // I'm not sure if the second (failed) registration simply doesn't end
58:         // up receiving wake up notifications, or there could be some race
59:         // condition when consuming readiness events, but having distinct
60:         // descriptors for distinct PollEvented instances appears to mitigate
61:         // this.
62:         //
63:         // Unfortunately we cannot just use a single global PollEvented instance
64:         // either, since we can't compare Handles or assume they will always
65:         // point to the exact same reactor.
66:         //
67:         // Mio 0.7 removed `try_clone()` as an API due to unexpected behavior
68:         // with registering dups with the same reactor. In this case, duping is
69:         // safe as each dup is registered with separate reactors **and** we
70:         // only expect at least one dup to receive the notification.
71: 
72:         // Manually drop as we don't actually own this instance of UnixStream.
73:         let signal_globals = globals();
74:         let receiver_fd = signal_globals.receiver.as_raw_fd();
75: 
76:         // safety: there is nothing unsafe about this, but the `from_raw_fd` fn is marked as unsafe.
77:         let original =
78:             ManuallyDrop::new(unsafe { std::os::unix::net::UnixStream::from_raw_fd(receiver_fd) });
79: 
80:         match original.try_clone() {
81:             Ok(std_receiver) => {
82:                 let mut mio_receiver = UnixStream::from_std(std_receiver);
83:                 let io_handle = park.handle();
84: 
85:                 let mut combined_interest: Option<Interest> = None;
86:                 for flag in [Interest::READABLE, Interest::WRITABLE] {
87:                     combined_interest = Some(match combined_interest {
88:                         Some(existing) => existing.add(flag),
89:                         None => flag,
90:                     });
91:                 }
92:                 let interest = combined_interest.expect("signal driver interest");
93: 
94:                 let allocated = {
95:                     let dispatcher = io_handle.inner.io_dispatch.read().unwrap();
96:                     if dispatcher.is_shutdown {
97:                         Err(io::Error::new(
98:                             io::ErrorKind::Other,
99:                             "failed to find event loop",
100:                         ))
101:                     } else {
102:                         let mut found = None;
103:                         for page in &dispatcher.allocator.pages[..] {
104:                             match Page::allocate(page) {
105:                                 Some(pair) => {
106:                                     found = Some(pair);
107:                                     break;
108:                                 }
109:                                 None => continue,
110:                             }
111:                         }
112:                         match found {
113:                             Some(pair) => Ok(pair),
114:                             None => Err(io::Error::new(
115:                                 io::ErrorKind::Other,
116:                                 "reactor at max registered I/O resources",
117:                             )),
118:                         }
119:                     }
120:                 };
121: 
122:                 match allocated {
123:                     Ok((address, shared)) => {
124:                         let generation = shared.generation();
125:                         let packed_address = ADDRESS.pack(address.as_usize(), 0);
126:                         let token = GENERATION.pack(generation, packed_address);
127:                         let mio_interest = interest.to_mio();
128:                         match io_handle.inner.registry.register(
129:                             &mut mio_receiver,
130:                             mio::Token(token),
131:                             mio_interest,
132:                         ) {
133:                             Ok(()) => {
134:                                 io_handle.inner.metrics.incr_fd_count();
135:                                 let registration = Registration {
136:                                     handle: io_handle,
137:                                     shared,
138:                                 };
139:                                 let receiver = PollEvented {
140:                                     io: Some(mio_receiver),
141:                                     registration,
142:                                 };
143:                                 Ok(Self {
144:                                     park,
145:                                     receiver,
146:                                     inner: Arc::new(Inner(())),
147:                                 })
148:                             }
149:                             Err(err) => Err(err),
150:                         }
151:                     }
152:                     Err(err) => Err(err),
153:                 }
154:             }
155:             Err(err) => Err(err),
156:         }
157:     }
158: 
159:     /// Returns a handle to this event loop which can be sent across threads
160:     /// and can be used as a proxy to the event loop itself.
161:     pub(crate) fn handle(&self) -> Handle {
162:         Handle {
163:             inner: Arc::downgrade(&self.inner),
164:         }
165:     }
166: 
167:     fn process(&self) {
168:         // Check if the pipe is ready to read and therefore has "woken" us up
169:         //
170:         // To do so, we will `poll_read_ready` with a noop waker, since we don't
171:         // need to actually be notified when read ready...
172:         let waker = unsafe { Waker::from_raw(RawWaker::new(ptr::null(), &NOOP_WAKER_VTABLE)) };
173:         let mut cx = Context::from_waker(&waker);
174: 
175:         let ev = match self.receiver.registration().poll_read_ready(&mut cx) {
176:             Poll::Ready(Ok(ev)) => ev,
177:             Poll::Ready(Err(e)) => panic!("reactor gone: {}", e),
178:             Poll::Pending => return, // No wake has arrived, bail
179:         };
180: 
181:         // Drain the pipe completely so we can receive a new readiness event
182:         // if another signal has come in.
183:         let mut buf = [0; 128];
184:         loop {
185:             match (&*self.receiver).read(&mut buf) {
186:                 Ok(0) => panic!("EOF on self-pipe"),
187:                 Ok(_) => continue, // Keep reading
188:                 Err(e) if e.kind() == io::ErrorKind::WouldBlock => break,
189:                 Err(e) => panic!("Bad read on self-pipe: {}", e),
190:             }
191:         }
192: 
193:         self.receiver.registration().clear_readiness(ev);
194: 
195:         // Broadcast any signals which were received
196:         globals().broadcast();
197:     }
198: }
199: 
200: const NOOP_WAKER_VTABLE: RawWakerVTable = RawWakerVTable::new(noop_clone, noop, noop, noop);
201: 
202: unsafe fn noop_clone(_data: *const ()) -> RawWaker {
203:     RawWaker::new(ptr::null(), &NOOP_WAKER_VTABLE)
204: }
205: 
206: unsafe fn noop(_data: *const ()) {}
207: 
208: // ===== impl Park for Driver =====
209: 
210: impl Park for Driver {
211:     type Unpark = <IoDriver as Park>::Unpark;
212:     type Error = io::Error;
213: 
214:     fn unpark(&self) -> Self::Unpark {
215:         self.park.unpark()
216:     }
217: 
218:     fn park(&mut self) -> Result<(), Self::Error> {
219:         self.park.park()?;
220:         self.process();
221:         Ok(())
222:     }
223: 
224:     fn park_timeout(&mut self, duration: Duration) -> Result<(), Self::Error> {
225:         self.park.park_timeout(duration)?;
226:         self.process();
227:         Ok(())
228:     }
229: 
230:     fn shutdown(&mut self) {
231:         self.park.shutdown()
232:     }
233: }
234: 
235: // ===== impl Handle =====
236: 
237: impl Handle {
238:     pub(super) fn check_inner(&self) -> io::Result<()> {
239:         if self.inner.strong_count() > 0 {
240:             Ok(())
241:         } else {
242:             Err(io::Error::new(io::ErrorKind::Other, "signal driver gone"))
243:         }
244:     }
245: }
246: 
247: cfg_rt! {
248:     impl Handle {
249:         /// Returns a handle to the current driver
250:         ///
251:         /// # Panics
252:         ///
253:         /// This function panics if there is no current signal driver set.
254:         #[track_caller]
255:         pub(super) fn current() -> Self {
256:             crate::runtime::context::signal_handle().expect(
257:                 "there is no signal driver running, must be called from the context of Tokio runtime",
258:             )
259:         }
260:     }
261: }
262: 
263: cfg_not_rt! {
264:     impl Handle {
265:         /// Returns a handle to the current driver
266:         ///
267:         /// # Panics
268:         ///
269:         /// This function panics if there is no current signal driver set.
270:         #[track_caller]
271:         pub(super) fn current() -> Self {
272:             panic!(
273:                 "there is no signal driver running, must be called from the context of Tokio runtime or with\
274:                 `rt` enabled.",
275:             )
276:         }
277:     }
278: }

part.text: Fixed. In `tokio/src/signal/unix/driver.rs:85`, the driver now registers only `Interest::READABLE` instead of combining `READABLE | WRITABLE`. Since the receiver self-pipe is never written, the always-writable descriptor was being reported ready on every poll iteration, causing a spin loop on level-triggered selectors. All signal test binaries (`signal*` tests) pass.
